cueManifest.exactScript: On go, stand, walk out, turn, walk back, and sit.
Five chair stands. Sit tall with arms crossed. On go, stand and sit five times, as quickly as feels safe.
Quick balance check. Fingertips near support, stand on your selected leg, and hold as long as comfortable.
Quick mobility check. Sit tall at the chair edge, one leg straight, and reach gently toward your toes.
Feet-together hold. Stand with feet together, fingertips near support, eyes open.
Single-leg hold. Stand on the approved leg, lift the other foot slightly, fingertips near support.
Tandem hold. Use the approved lead foot, heel to toe, fingertips near support.
Band pull-apart. Hold a light band at chest height. Pull your hands wide, then return slowly.
Supported split squat. Use the approved stance side, fingertips near support. Bend both knees slightly, then stand tall.
Bridge hold. Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Lift your hips and hold.
Glute bridge. Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Lift your hips, then lower with control.
Heel raise. Stand tall. Rise onto the balls of your feet, then lower slowly.
Supported heel raise. Fingertips near support. Rise onto the balls of your feet, then lower slowly.
Hip hinge. Feet under hips. Send hips back with a long spine, then stand tall.
Wall-tap hinge. Stand a step from the wall. Send hips back to tap the wall, then stand tall.
March in place. Stand tall near support and march with a steady rhythm.
Loaded sit-to-stand. Hold the load close to your chest. Stand fully, then sit with control.
Mini-band lateral walk. Place the mini band above your knees. Take small controlled side steps.
Neck rotations. Face the phone, sit or stand tall, and slowly look over one shoulder, then the other.
Band overhead press. Stand tall with light band tension. Press overhead, then return slowly.
Overhead reach. Stand tall. Reach both arms overhead as far as comfortable, then lower.
Incline push-up. Hands on a stable counter or sturdy chair. Lower in with control, then press away.
Push-up. Hands under your shoulders. Lower with control, then press up.
Wall push-up. Hands on the wall. Lower in with control, then press away.
Seated band row. Sit tall with the band secure under your feet or a low anchor. Pull elbows back, then return slowly.
Seated hamstring reach. Sit tall at the chair edge, one leg straight. Reach gently toward your toes and hold.
Squat. Feet about hip width. Lower as if to sit, then stand with control.
Loaded squat. Hold the load close to your chest. Lower into a squat, then stand with control.
Slow-lower squat. Lower slowly, then stand with control.
Supported squat. Stand near sturdy support. Lower as if to sit, then stand with control.
Standing band row. Face the anchored band with a stable stance. Pull elbows back, then return slowly.
Step-up. Use the approved leading foot. Step up, bring the other foot to meet it, then step down leading with the same foot.
Cushion sit-to-stand. Sit tall on the cushion, feet flat. Stand fully, then sit with control.
Power sit-to-stand. Sit tall, drive up briskly to standing, then sit with control.
Slow-lower sit-to-stand. Stand fully, then lower slowly and steadily before the next rep.
Sit-to-stand. Sit tall in the middle of the chair, feet flat. Stand fully, then sit with control.
Supported hip-flexor stretch. Use the approved stance side, fingertips near support. Shift forward gently and hold.
Supported side step. Stand near a counter. Step to the side, bring the other foot in, and continue with control.
Thoracic rotation. Sit or stand tall with arms crossed. Rotate one way, return to center, then rotate the other way.
Supported toe raise. Keep heels down, lift the front of your feet, then lower slowly.
Wall calf stretch. Hands on the wall, approved leg back, heel down. Lean forward gently and hold.

founderDecisions.question: How should unilateral or asymmetric training work be balanced inside a session?
founderDecisions.whyItMatters: Odd set counts and unspecified sides can give one side more work while the voice sounds authoritative.
founderDecisions.currentProductionBehavior: Single-leg, tandem, step-up, split stance, seated reach, hip-flexor stretch, and calf stretch do not persist or encode a side schedule in the training registry.
options: Define a round as both sides completed before advancing.
Use even side-specific sets where the architecture cannot express both sides in one round.
Leave side choice to the user and mark these as non-comparable practice only.
founderDecisions.codexRecommendation: Define equal left/right work within a round; until implemented, avoid freezing side-specific scripts for affected items.
founderDecisions.safeDefault: Do not assign left-right-left. Block side-specific scripts and keep current programming unchanged.
founderDecisions.consequences: Requires training state and session-player side context before reliable voice-first side cues.

founderDecisions.question: How should baseline measurement side be selected and persisted for official measurements and micro-checks?
founderDecisions.whyItMatters: Shoulder, hinge, single-leg balance, and mobility micro-checks cannot claim same-side comparability without persisted side metadata.
founderDecisions.currentProductionBehavior: Legacy graders dynamically choose reliable near side; Movement Profile V2 setup types can carry standingLeg/selectedSide but default legacy battery does not persist side.
options: Use reliable comfortable side at baseline, persist it, and retest the same side.
Hard-code left side for all official measurements.
Allow either side but mark reduced comparability when side changes.
founderDecisions.codexRecommendation: Use reliable comfortable side at baseline, persist exact side, retest same side, and mark reduced comparability for fallback.
founderDecisions.safeDefault: Do not claim same-side comparability until side persistence exists.
founderDecisions.consequences: Requires result schema/protocol-version work and side-aware setup copy.

founderDecisions.question: Should eyes-closed balance remain in an unsupervised default home check-up?
founderDecisions.whyItMatters: Current default balance ladder includes eyes-closed feet-together and tandem stages, which may be a safety/protocol issue for home use.
founderDecisions.currentProductionBehavior: DEFAULT_BALANCE_STAGES includes feet-together eyes closed and tandem eyes closed; training safety explicitly says eyes open.
options: Keep eyes-closed stages with explicit safety approval and support wording.
Move eyes-closed stages to supervised or optional protocol.
Remove eyes-closed stages from default home check-up.
founderDecisions.codexRecommendation: Do not expand or remove in this task; require explicit founder/protocol approval before script freeze.
founderDecisions.safeDefault: Block eyes-closed script freeze while preserving current production behavior.
founderDecisions.consequences: May require balance protocol versioning and scoring expectations.

founderDecisions.question: Where should the mini band be placed for the initial lateral-walk level?
founderDecisions.whyItMatters: Current visible copy allows above knees or around ankles; the voice needs one unambiguous safe setup.
founderDecisions.currentProductionBehavior: ladders.ts says above knees or around ankles; exercise definition only requires mini_band and timed movement.
options: Above knees for initial level.
Around ankles as a harder variation.
Let user choose and mark as non-standard.
founderDecisions.codexRecommendation: Use above knees for the initial level; treat ankle placement as a later progression.
founderDecisions.safeDefault: Above knees, but block script freeze until founder approves.
founderDecisions.consequences: May require ladder copy and future progression naming.

founderDecisions.question: What are step-up rep semantics and the leg-switch schedule?
founderDecisions.whyItMatters: Current step-up target is 12 total accepted reps across three sets, while the spoken copy says lead down with the same foot and production does not balance sides.
founderDecisions.currentProductionBehavior: step-up has three sets of 12 reps, one reliable side chain, and no side state.
options: Alternate legs within each set and count total reps.
Use side-specific sets with an even set count.
Keep one leading leg and classify as non-balanced practice.
founderDecisions.codexRecommendation: Alternate legs within the set if the grader can support it; otherwise use even side-specific sets.
founderDecisions.safeDefault: Block final step-up script; do not invent left-right-left.
founderDecisions.consequences: May require grader/session-player side semantics and prescription update in a later authorised task.

founderDecisions.question: Should set count be spoken on first exposure?
founderDecisions.whyItMatters: Set-plan lines add narration but are not needed to perform the immediate set.
founderDecisions.currentProductionBehavior: The player does not speak set count on first exposure; it speaks rest and last-set transitions.
options: Do not speak set count by default.
Speak set count only on first ever exposure.
Speak set count for every exercise.
founderDecisions.codexRecommendation: Do not speak set count by default.
founderDecisions.safeDefault: Omit set-plan assets from V2 active surface.
founderDecisions.consequences: Keeps first-use timelines shorter and reduces asset count.

founderDecisions.question: Do floor exercises require an explicit transfer-readiness gate or only concise setup copy?
founderDecisions.whyItMatters: Floor work can be safe for some users and inappropriate for others; a voice line alone cannot solve transfer readiness.
founderDecisions.currentProductionBehavior: Floor exercises have setup/active safety cues but no separate readiness gate.
options: Add a transfer-readiness gate before floor work.
Keep concise copy and rely on equipment/capability filtering.
Remove floor work from default blocks.
founderDecisions.codexRecommendation: Add a transfer-readiness gate before broad rollout; keep floor scripts blocked until approved.
founderDecisions.safeDefault: Do not promise floor transfer support in voice copy; block floor-exercise script freeze.
founderDecisions.consequences: May require profile capability flow and exercise substitution rules.
